The `new_state` is `None` when the entity is removed.

Suggested alternate fix:
```
diff --git a/homeassistant/components/filter/sensor.py b/homeassistant/components/filter/sensor.py
index d46709924e..a448d1657c 100644
--- a/homeassistant/components/filter/sensor.py
+++ b/homeassistant/components/filter/sensor.py
@@ -195,7 +195,9 @@ class SensorFilter(Entity):
     def _update_filter_sensor_state_event(self, event):
         """Handle device state changes."""
         _LOGGER.debug("Update filter on event: %s", event)
-        self._update_filter_sensor_state(event.data.get("new_state"))
+        new_state = event.data.get("new_state")
+        if new_state is not None:
+            self._update_filter_sensor_state(new_state)
 
     @callback
     def _update_filter_sensor_state(self, new_state, update_ha=True):
```

> @bdraco `_update_filter_sensor_state` already checks if state is `None`

It does on `dev`: It looks like you already fixed this problem in #44439

So, I guess most of us are confused with the issue that is left (and not fixed by #44439).

Could you add a test that shows the need for this addition at this point?
At least the history component provides `LazyState` which can be `None`
Right, so that sounds like a bug. In that case we shouldn't work around the bug but instead fix the bug.
Should we remove `LazyState` and make it `State` ?
The history integration works with `State` because it will only parse data when accessed. We should keep it that way.
I'm closing this in favour of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/45644 and of all the other PR that have tackled other cases

issue_context.body:

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Here is my configuration.yaml:

```
default_config:

http:
  base_url: https://nottherealsiteurl.org
  ssl_certificate: /ssl/fullchain.pem
  ssl_key: /ssl/privkey.pem

# Text to speech
tts:
  - platform: google_translate

sensor:
  - platform: filter
    name: "Crawlspace 7 day average humidity"
    entity_id: sensor.crawlspace_humidity
    filters:
      - filter: time_simple_moving_average
        window_size: "168:00"

automation: !include automations.yaml
script: !include scripts.yaml

```

When I start home assistant I see:

```


Logger: homeassistant.components.sensor
Source: components/filter/sensor.py:333
Integration: Sensor (documentation, issues)
First occurred: October 3, 2020, 5:09:32 PM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: October 3, 2020, 5:09:32 PM
Error while setting up filter platform for sensor

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 201, in _async_setup_platform
    await asyncio.gather(*pending)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 310, in async_add_entities
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 481, in _async_add_entity
    await entity.add_to_platform_finish()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 521, in add_to_platform_finish
    await self.async_added_to_hass()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/filter/sensor.py", line 286, in async_added_to_hass
    self._update_filter_sensor_state(state, False)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/filter/sensor.py", line 197, in _update_filter_sensor_state
    filtered_state = filt.filter_state(copy(temp_state))
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/filter/sensor.py", line 403, in filter_state
    fstate = FilterState(new_state)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/filter/sensor.py", line 333, in __init__
    self.state = float(state.state)
TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a number, not 'NoneType'

```

When I remove this portion of the config and restart I see no error.

```
sensor:
  - platform: filter
    name: "Crawlspace 7 day average humidity"
    entity_id: sensor.crawlspace_humidity
    filters:
      - filter: time_simple_moving_average
        window_size: "168:00"
```

* I can confirm this was working with  0.114.
* All versions of the config validate with `ha core check`
* yamllint.com says all of my config is valid.



## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->
I'm running hass.io on a Raspberry Pi 3+ with  0.115.6.
comments:
Strangely, if I set the `window_size` to `"00:05" as in [this example](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/filter/#configuration) it reboots without error and I can see the `sensor` entity created by the filter. That working config snippet would be:

```
sensor:
  - platform: filter
    name: "Crawlspace 7 day average humidity"
    entity_id: sensor.crawlspace_humidity
    filters:
      - filter: time_simple_moving_average
        window_size: "00:05"
```

Hey there @dgomes, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`filter`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L137) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
What is ```window_size: "168:00"``` supposed to mean ? that is not a valid time...

> What is `window_size: "168:00"` supposed to mean ? that is not a valid time...

It's intended to be a 7-day filter. 7 days is 168 hours. How can I express a 7-day moving average window size?

`window_size` is of **time period** in HA, therefore you can easily define 7 days like:

```
sensor:
  - platform: filter
    name: "Crawlspace 7 day average humidity"
    entity_id: sensor.crawlspace_humidity
    filters:
      - filter: time_simple_moving_average
        window_size: 
          days: 7
Another aspect: do you keep more then 7 days of history in your recorder ? because if you don't you will get an error...

Thanks for the info on the window_size! I use the default history of 10 days so this shouldn't be an issue. When I apply the `days: 7` option though I get the same error: `TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a number, not 'NoneType'`.

I believe that what I'm seeing is that this error is due to the data in my db somehow being inaccurate. I can try to sort that out, but when a value in the time series is not a number, can we ignore it an have it keep computing? What do you think can be improved to help out a situation like this?
if it's now a number, we always ignore it. Issue is usually around "bad numbers"

The reproducer I would describe is around adding a new sensor for example. If I add a new sensor and ask it for a `days: 7` moving average the sensor component filter sensor component fails to start. Once 7 days have passed, it will start, no problem.
But that's the expected behaviour. If you need 7 days moving average it takes exactly 7 days to achieve that average...

Logically speaking, yes this is expected. Practically speaking, this is problematic for example in these two situations:

1. A power outage occurs and data is not posted for even a few minutes. Then restart hass, observe the component fails to start.
2. You are setting up a new sensor, you don't yet have all the data, the filter component fails to start even though everything is configured properly.

I'm motivating the case that it shouldbe possible to handle a lack of data as NaN and the filter component should still start. We don't need to agree on a single way to do it, this could be parametrized. For example, in many statistics softwares these summarizations typically have a parameter on how to handle NaN's. I believe they rarely "just fail" without any recourse for the user.

1. If sensor skips a value, the SMA Filter handles that without any issue

2. Can you post some debug info showing the sensor fails ?

I've just created a sensor in my test environment with the same configuration of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/41224#issuecomment-703637909

It created the sensor without any **error**

> What integration is sensor.crawlspace_humidity ?

It's an esphome DHT22 sensor. This uses the esphome add on, which creates the devices. Here's the esphome config for example:

```

  name: crawlspace
  platform: ESP8266
  board: nodemcuv2

wifi:
  ssid: "network_name"
  password: "password"

  # Enable fallback hotspot (captive portal) in case wifi connection fails
  ap:
    ssid: "Crawlspace Fallback Hotspot"
    password: "anotherpassword"

captive_portal:

# Enable logging
logger:

# Enable Home Assistant API
api:

ota:

sensor:
  - platform: dht
    model: DHT22
    pin: D7
    temperature:
      name: "Crawlspace Temperature"
    humidity:
      name: "Crawlspace Humidity"
```

Also, apologies for the loooong delay to reply. I'll try to respond quicker next time.
> Can you post some debug info showing the sensor fails ?

It hasn't occured in a week or two. It happened last time during a power loss. From the UI I see it say the entity the esphome sensor produces is "unavailable". It has happened 4 times now so I'm sure it'll happen again. What data should I gather specifically that would be helpful?

You said:

> 2. You are setting up a new sensor, you don't yet have all the data, the filter component fails to start even though everything is configured properly.

I could not reproduce such error, so I'm asking for logs showing the error
I see, so just the home assistant logs. Those have aged out on the system, but when it happens again (I'm sure it will) I will post them.

In this case I have a filter over a very simple template sensor `{{ 1000 }}`
I've opened a new issue, this has nothing to do with history, its event change and can be replicated using template as in #43457

Actually got a test that shows that when template is reloaded the all "State" becomes None:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/44439/files#diff-979128f340f102ef3e390c796f36715b5e5c713a4965f4d4ccba42f932fc9befR139

In a more recent Issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/44424

The log shows the `None` comes from the history component `(None, datetime.datetime(2020, 12, 22, 12, 33, 27, 677473, tzinfo=<UTC>))`

When you query the `history` integration it does not return `State` but a `LazyState` https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/68221907729405836890e56a879e363b1c003510/homeassistant/components/history/__init__.py#L338

And LazyState can in fact be None...

So can we move this forward :) ? I think this PR is appropriate considering the specific use of history component...
